facts.statement: The genus Plesiocathartes was originally described by Gaillard in 1908.
The type species of the genus is Plesiocathartes europaeus.
Five species are currently recognized within the genus, including P. gaillardi, P. major, P. insolitipes, P. kelleri, and P. wyomingensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. gaillardi Crusafont & Villalta, 1955 P. major Weidig, 2006 P. insolitipes Mayr & Kitchener, 2022 P. kelleri Mayr, 2002 P. wyomingensis Weidig, 2006

facts.statement: Plesiocathartes is an extinct genus of birds.
facts.quote: Plesiocathartes is an extinct genus of birds

facts.statement: Fossils of the genus have been found in Europe and North America.
facts.quote: It currently presents 5 species from Europe and North America

facts.statement: The genus is classified within the order Leptosomiformes.
The genus lived from the Ypresian to the Rupelian stages, approximately 56 to 27.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Rupelian (56 to 27.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are four recorded fossil occurrences of the genus in the Paleobiology Database.
Fossils of P. insolitipes have been found at Walton-on-the-Naze in the London Clay Formation of southeastern England.
facts.quote: P. insolitipes fossils are known from Walton-on-the-Naze, a site stratigraphically located in the Walton Member of the London Clay Formation of southeastern England
